# L1 fact matrix: Claude Code and Codex

<!-- Generated by `bun run --cwd packages/api-routes facts:matrix` from packages/api-routes/src/session-transcript/transcript-records/fact-catalog.ts. Do not edit by hand: change the catalog and regenerate. -->

Every literal fact L1 knows about, what Claude Code and Codex each record for it, and what Opaline stores today. The columns are defined in the [L1 literal schema](l1-literal-schema.md); the catalog behind this page is checked by tests, and the drift census (`bun run --cwd packages/api-routes facts:census -- <transcripts>`) lists transcript fields no row accounts for.

## Legend

- ✅ **stored**: Opaline stores it. `v6` is the transcript parser version that first stored it; `elsewhere` means another table (usage, run index, git observations), named in the details.
- ✅ … **+ gap**: stored, but the agent also records it in a place we do not read yet; the details say where and which change will read it.
- 🟡 **pending**: the agent records it and we do not store it yet; the details name the change that will (`parser 9` is the next transcript parser version).
- ⚪ **not recorded**: the agent does not write it; the details say how that was checked.
- 🔴 **wrong**: stored, but known to be incorrect; the details say what is wrong and the fix.

"Local census" in the details is the census of the local transcripts, 2026-10-09: 275 Claude Code files (2.1.220–2.1.293, 163,945 records) and 2,694 Codex files (0.100–0.162, 3,055,210 records); "locally" counts are from it too.

Under each status is where the agent records the fact, shortened: `toolUseResult.x` is a field of a Claude Code tool result, `Bash input.x` a tool call's argument, `exec_command args.x` a Codex call's argument, `CommandExecution.x` a field of a Codex completed item, `output “…”` a convention at the start of a call's output text. `{*}` stands for a key that is data (a file path, an id, a model name).

## Summary

| | Claude Code | Codex |
|---|---:|---:|
| ✅ stored | 76 (13 with a gap) | 52 (20 with a gap) |
| 🟡 pending | 32 | 36 |
| ⚪ not recorded | 20 | 34 |
| 🔴 wrong | 2 | 8 |
| Facts | 130 | 130 |

## Decisions needed

1. **`file_op`** (calls): Should a file change the agent asked for but no result confirms (a refused or failed edit, a shell `rm` that may have found nothing) count as an edit, or only changes a result confirms?
2. **`permission_decision`** (calls): Does a permission accepted by configuration (Claude `source: config`, `reasonType: mode`; Codex approved command prefixes) count as an approval, or only a decision a person made at the time (`user_temporary`, a Codex approval prompt)?
3. **`service_tier`** (runs): Codex responses record no service tier, only the thread's configured one (`thread_settings_applied`). Should Codex usage be priced at the configured tier?
4. **`instruction_sha256`** (prompts): Should instruction_sha256 hash the instruction text as the agent received it (what the model saw), or only repository files from CLI captures?

### Details

- `tool_name`
  - Codex ✅: Note: A connector tool's name (`_create_pull_request`) does not say which app it belongs to; see tool_namespace. All sources: `function_call.name`, `custom_tool_call.name`, `web_search_call.action.type`, `McpToolCall.tool`, `DynamicToolCall.tool`.
- `call_id`
  - Codex ✅: All sources: `function_call.call_id`, `custom_tool_call.call_id`, `function_call_output.call_id`, `custom_tool_call_output.call_id`, `completed item.id`, `exec_command_end.call_id`, `patch_apply_end.call_id`.
- `input_text`
  - Codex ✅: All sources: `exec_command args.cmd`, `shell args.command[]`, `function_call.arguments`, `custom_tool_call.input`, `CommandExecution.command[]`.
- `command_argv0`, `command_prefix`
  - Claude Code 🟡: Plan: find over calls (order of work step 10) derives it from the stored command text; no parser change
  - Codex 🟡: Plan: find over calls (order of work step 10) derives it from the stored command text; no parser change
- `command_fingerprint`, `command_simhash`
  - Claude Code 🟡: Plan: find over calls (order of work step 10) derives it from the stored command text; no parser change
  - Codex 🟡: Plan: find over calls (order of work step 10) derives it from the stored command text; no parser change
- `is_error`
  - Claude Code ✅: Note: Stored as not failed when the result has no `is_error`, which is an inference: 5,519 results locally (19%, mostly Read, Edit, Write and WebFetch) have none, and only 4 of them read like an error.
  - Codex 🔴: Fix: parser 9: a call Codex refused or could not run (`exec_command failed …`, `write_stdin failed …`, `failed to parse function arguments`, a view_image call's `unable to locate image at …`) is stored as not failed today; record that transport failure as a failure (locally: 108 refusals, 634 other `… failed` outputs, 50 `failed to parse function arguments`, 38 `unable to locate image at`). Note: Not comparable across agents: Codex marks every nonzero exit a failure (grep or diff finding nothing included); Claude Code marks a nonzero exit not failed only when it gives a return_code_interpretation (170 results locally: 168 `No matches found`, 2 `Files differ`), and every other one failed (`Exit code N`). All sources: `CommandExecution.exit_code`, `completed item.status`, `exec_command_end.exit_code`, `patch_apply_end.success`, `McpToolCall.result.isError`, `output “Process exited with code…”`, `output “failed…”`, `output “failed to parse function arguments…”`, `output “unable to locate image at…”`.
- `exit_code`
  - Claude Code ✅: Note: Claude Code writes an exit code only into the text of a failed result (`Exit code 1`); successful calls have none.
  - Codex 🔴: Fix: parser 9: when a command's completion arrives after its output said it was still running, the call stays `running` with no exit code and the completion row keeps neither; keep the completion's exit code and status on its row (locally 19,520 late completions, 4,324 of them nonzero). All sources: `CommandExecution.exit_code`, `exec_command_end.exit_code`, `output “Process exited with code…”`, `output “Exit code…”`, `output.metadata.exit_code`.
- `denial_kind`
  - Claude Code ✅: Note: `permission-rule` also covers calls a hook denied; permission_decision's `source` tells them apart.
  - Codex ✅: Note: Codex writes no denial field; the refusal is the call's output (`exec_command failed …: CreateProcess { message: "Rejected(…` or `Codex(Sandbox(Denied …`).
  - Run index columns: `denied_calls`.
- `denial_reason`
  - Claude Code 🟡: Plan: parser 9: keep the string `toolUseResult` of a refused or blocked result (worktree isolation, `Blocked: sleep`), and the phase, tool and message of a `PreToolUse:<tool> hook error` result.
  - Codex 🔴: Fix: parser 9: a reason over 512 characters is cut without `facts_clipped`, and the cut can drop the policy explanation that follows the command (7 refusals locally); cap it with the clipping-aware setter so the cut is marked.
- `return_code_interpretation`
  - Codex ⚪: How we checked: local census: no field or output convention interprets an exit code (searched CommandExecution, exec_command_end and every call output prefix).
- `duration_ms`
  - Claude Code ✅: Note: Only some tools record it (web fetch and search, a few others); shell results record none.
  - Codex ✅: Gap: also recorded at `DynamicToolCall.duration.*`. Plan: parser 9: the dynamic tool handler keeps its recorded duration. Note: Versions without CommandExecution items (0.100, 0.105, 0.108–0.118 and 0.130–0.145 locally) record no command duration; see wall_time_ms. All sources: `CommandExecution.duration.*`, `McpToolCall.duration.*`, `exec_command_end.duration.*`.
- `wall_time_ms`
  - Claude Code ⚪: How we checked: local census: no wait time is written into Claude Code results.
  - Codex 🟡: Plan: parser 9: keep the output framing's `Wall time` and the envelope's `duration_seconds` as transport time, apart from duration_ms. Note: A poll of a background command reports only its own wait.
- `call_started_at`, `call_completed_at`
  - Claude Code ⚪: How we checked: local census: tool results carry no start or end time of their own; only the record timestamps.
  - Codex 🟡: Plan: parser 9: keep the completion's recorded start and end on its row.
